title: New Hampshire Paycheck Calculator 2026 – Take-Home Pay

heading: New Hampshire Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free New Hampshire paycheck calculator to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare and employee benefit deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your deductions to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

New Hampshire does not impose personal income tax on ordinary employment wages. However, federal payroll taxes and employee benefits still affect the amount deposited into your bank account.

Whether you work in Manchester, Nashua, Concord, Portsmouth or another New Hampshire community, understanding your net earnings can help you compare employment opportunities and manage household expenses.

## How to Use the New Hampshire Paycheck Calculator

Begin by choosing whether you receive a fixed salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross income before taxes and select your payment frequency. Hourly employees should include regular working hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Enter the federal income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Add retirement contributions, health insurance premiums and other employee deductions. Include any additional federal withholding in the federal total.

If you are approaching the annual Social Security wage ceiling or Additional Medicare withholding threshold, include your year-to-date taxable earnings.

Review your estimated gross income, individual payroll deductions and net paycheck.

New Hampshire employees generally do not need to complete a separate state income tax withholding certificate for ordinary employment within the state.

## New Hampshire Payroll Taxes in 2026

Although New Hampshire does not impose individual wage income tax, employees may still face federal payroll deductions.

Your actual take-home earnings depend on federal withholding elections, taxable wages, employment classification and employee benefits.

Employees working across state borders may have additional withholding obligations.

## Does New Hampshire Have State Income Tax?

New Hampshire does not impose individual income tax on ordinary W-2 wages.

Employees working and residing in New Hampshire generally do not have a New Hampshire personal income tax deduction on their regular paychecks.

This differs from neighboring states such as Massachusetts, Maine and Vermont, which impose individual income taxes.

However, the absence of a state wage income tax does not mean your entire gross salary becomes take-home pay.

Federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare, health insurance and retirement contributions may still reduce your paycheck considerably.

Read the official [New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration tax guidance](https://www.revenue.nh.gov/) for information about the state's individual income tax treatment.

## New Hampshire Interest and Dividends Tax Repeal

New Hampshire previously imposed a separate tax on qualifying interest and dividend income.

This was different from a wage income tax and generally did not apply to ordinary employee salaries.

The Interest and Dividends Tax was repealed for taxable periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025.

Consequently, a 2026 New Hampshire paycheck calculator should not deduct this former tax from employment earnings.

The repeal does not eliminate federal income tax obligations on qualifying investment income or liabilities from earlier applicable tax periods.

The official [New Hampshire tax repeal announcement](https://www.revenue.nh.gov/taxes-glance/interest-dividends-tax) explains the transition.

## Federal Income Tax on New Hampshire Paychecks

Your employer generally calculates federal income tax withholding using your taxable earnings and the information provided on Form W-4.

The calculation considers your filing status, payment frequency, multiple jobs, eligible tax credits, other income and requested additional withholding.

Federal income tax is progressive. Different portions of taxable income may be subject to different rates.

Multiplying your entire gross salary by your highest marginal federal tax rate will generally produce an inaccurate estimate.

Employers follow the withholding procedures described in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

The amount withheld is an advance payment toward your annual federal income tax liability. Your final return may result in a refund or additional tax due.

## Social Security and Medicare Contributions


### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages toward Social Security.

The 2026 annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500.

For example, an employee earning $2,500 in covered wages who has not reached the annual limit would contribute $155.

Employees earning above the annual wage ceiling may notice an increase in take-home pay once their employer stops collecting ordinary Social Security contributions for the remainder of the year.

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding is 1.45% of covered earnings.

A paycheck containing $2,500 in Medicare-covered wages would produce a $36.25 deduction.

Unlike Social Security, ordinary Medicare withholding does not have a standard annual wage ceiling.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% when covered Medicare wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Consult the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for additional payroll tax information.

## New Hampshire Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually and receiving 26 biweekly paychecks.
Assume the employee is single for federal withholding purposes, uses a modern Form W-4, has no additional credits or withholding adjustments and has not reached annual payroll contribution limits.

This example assumes no retirement contributions, healthcare premiums or other employee deductions.

An employee with different withholding elections or benefit arrangements may receive a different net paycheck despite earning the same annual salary.

## New Hampshire Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate gross earnings by multiplying their hourly wage by regular working hours and adding qualifying overtime compensation.

Suppose an employee earns $28 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$28 × 40 = $1,120

Overtime earnings:

$28 × 1.5 × 6 = $252

Total gross earnings:

$1,372

Assuming all wages are subject to ordinary federal payroll contributions, Social Security would be approximately $85.06 and Medicare would be approximately $19.89.

Federal income tax and other employee deductions would also apply.

Review the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) to understand overtime eligibility and exemptions.

## Working in Massachusetts While Living in New Hampshire

Many residents of southern New Hampshire commute to Massachusetts for employment.

Although New Hampshire does not tax ordinary wages, Massachusetts may impose income tax on employment earnings sourced to Massachusetts.

Living in Nashua while working in Boston, for example, does not automatically eliminate Massachusetts withholding.

Remote employees and workers performing duties in multiple states may need to allocate earnings according to applicable income sourcing rules.

Consult the [Massachusetts Department of Revenue](https://www.mass.gov/orgs/massachusetts-department-of-revenue) before treating interstate employment income as exempt from state withholding.

A standard New Hampshire paycheck estimate is most appropriate for ordinary employment without additional out-of-state tax obligations.

## Employee Benefits and Your New Hampshire Paycheck

Your employer may deduct contributions toward retirement savings, healthcare coverage, insurance and other benefits.

Traditional 401(k) contributions generally reduce current federal income-taxable wages, while Roth contributions generally do not provide the same immediate income tax reduction.

Qualifying health insurance arrangements may reduce certain taxable wage amounts.

New Hampshire also has a voluntary paid family and medical leave insurance program. Employees participating in coverage may have insurance-related payroll deductions depending on their arrangements.

Visit the official [New Hampshire Paid Family and Medical Leave website](https://www.paidfamilymedicalleave.nh.gov/) for program information.

Do not assume every employee pays the same insurance premium or participates in the program.

## Comparing New Hampshire Salaries With Other States

When comparing employment opportunities, consider the complete financial picture.

A position in New Hampshire may provide higher take-home income than an identical salary in a state that imposes wage income tax.

However, differences in housing costs, property taxes, commuting expenses and employee benefits may reduce or outweigh that advantage.

Use our [US paycheck calculator](/calculators/paycheck-calculator/) to compare estimated salaries across state borders.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish an appropriate savings target, while our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help evaluate different compensation arrangements.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Does New Hampshire deduct state income tax from paychecks?

No. New Hampshire does not impose individual income tax on ordinary W-2 wages. Federal taxes and other employee deductions may still apply.

### Do New Hampshire residents working in Massachusetts pay Massachusetts income tax?

They may owe Massachusetts income tax on qualifying employment earnings sourced to Massachusetts, despite living in a state without wage income tax.

### Does New Hampshire still have an interest and dividends tax?

The former Interest and Dividends Tax was repealed for taxable periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025.
